# Physical Activity for Recovery Stability

Physical activity is a key support for recovery. It helps regulate the body and mind by:

-   Lowering stress hormones
-   Improving sleep quality
-   Lifting mood and energy
-   Reducing craving intensity for many people

Importantly, you do **not** need intense or time-consuming workouts. Consistency is more important than intensity.

Even brief movement can help interrupt urge cycles by:

-   Shifting your attention
-   Changing your physical state
-   Creating distance from automatic reactions

Over time, regular activity builds resilience, routine, and a reliable alternative to using alcohol.

![](https://github.com/jjcurtin/aud_support/blob/main/modules/images/bike.jpg?raw=true){fig-align="center"}

## Build Your Activity Menu

Create a range of options so you have something to match your energy and situation.

| Low-effort options (5-15 min) | Moderate options (20-40 min) | Social options |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
|                               |                              |                |
|                               |                              |                |
|                               |                              |                |

*Tip: Include options you can do at home, outside, and in different weather or moods.*

::: callout-tip
### Skill rehearsal

Think of this as practice for real-life moments when motivation is low and urges are high.

-   Schedule three activity sessions this week (At least one from each column).

-   Treat each session as a planned response, not just exercise

-   Focus on showing up, not doing it perfectly

-   If motivation is low, start smaller (even 5 minutes). Starting is the most important step.

**Remember: Repetition builds confidence and makes healthy responses easier to access under stress.**
:::
